summary: Reactive Spring Cloud Gateway edge service: 4 Java classes, 1 YAML, 0 tests. No JWT library is present or used - bearer-token validation is delegated over HTTP to service-id 'service-users' by one AbstractGatewayFilterFactory (AuthFilter). No route is declared in this component at all; config-service serves the table and attaches AuthFilter to 2 of 3 routes. HIGH-CONFIDENCE DEFECT: routes target lb://user-service while AuthFilter calls http://service-users - two ids for one service, so the auth hop probably cannot resolve.

answers.d_whatProducesThe401: Nothing - there is no 401 in this module. A missing header (AuthFilter.java:24) or a malformed Bearer value (:32) throws a bare RuntimeException inside the filter chain; with no ErrorWebExceptionHandler, @ControllerAdvice or SecurityWebFilter present, WebFlux's default error handling renders that as HTTP 500 with a Boot default JSON body. A downstream 401 from /users/validateToken surfaces as WebClientResponseException from .retrieve() and likewise becomes 500. So an expired or invalid token yields 500, never 401 - and it is NOT dead code: the hand-off shows AuthFilter is attached to /users/** and /persons/**. Inferred from code + reactive-stack defaults; not observed at runtime.
answers.e_hardcodedBaseUrl: One Java literal: "http://service-users/users/validateToken" (AuthFilter.java:37) - hard-coded scheme AND service-id, not an 'lb://' URI, not injected from configuration; because the builder is @LoadBalanced the host is still resolved through Consul Discovery, so it is not a fixed host:port. The inconsistency is the finding: the route table uses the canonical lb://user-service form while this filter hand-builds http://service-users - two ids for one service. Second literal: http://localhost:8888/ at bootstrap.yml:3 (CONFIG_SERVER env-overridable). No external internet URL exists in this module.

recommendations: P1 defect - AuthFilter.java:40-42: the mutate() result is dropped and the X-auth-user-id header line is commented out, so the authenticated identity never reaches any downstream service. Rebuild as exchange.getRequest().mutate().header("X-auth-user-id", String.valueOf(userDto.getId())).build() and pass the MUTATED exchange into the chain.

P1 defect - answer 401, not 500: replace both 'throw new RuntimeException(...)' (AuthFilter.java:24, :32) with a typed exception plus an ErrorWebExceptionHandler that writes 401 for missing/malformed tokens and maps WebClientResponseException.Unauthorized from the validation call to 401 too.

P1 security - take the bearer token out of the query string (AuthFilter.java:37) and send it as the downstream Authorization header; add explicit onStatus handling instead of relying on .retrieve(), plus a timeout, so an unavailable user-service degrades cleanly instead of hanging the edge.

P1 correctness - reconcile the literal service-id 'service-users' (AuthFilter.java:37) with the actual registered name of user-service before any release. The route table already targets lb://user-service, so the gateway uses two ids for one service; if they differ there is no working authenticated path in the platform.

P1 security (confirm in gateway-service.yml) - spring.cloud.gateway.discovery.locator.enabled: true turns the 3-route table into a convenience list rather than an allow-list: any Consul-registered service is reachable under /{service-id}/** with NO AuthFilter. Disable or constrain the locator.

P2 - delete the three commented dependency blocks (pom.xml:49-53, :55-59, :61-64). They are the direct cause of Phase 3 attributing jjwt 0.9.1, java-jwt 4.2.1 and spring-boot-starter-security to this module; correct .opencode/rules/development.md:42 and .opencode/project_init.md:220 - this gateway is a token RELAY, not a validator.

P2 - pom.xml:106-107 sets maven-compiler source/target 10 while the parent declares java.version 17 (root pom.xml:31). Drop the explicit 10/10 so the module stops compiling to a different bytecode level from the reactor.
P2 - drop the unused commons-lang3 dependency (pom.xml:66-69): zero imports in the module.

P2 - add the first test. 4 classes, the sole authentication gate for the platform, 0 tests. One WebTestClient test proving 401-without-token and 200-with-valid-token pins exactly what the fixes above change. Also add logging - a rejected request currently leaves no trace.

P2 - declare routes in-tree (a local application.yml or a Java RouteLocator bean) and leave config-service for environment-specific overrides; today this component cannot be reviewed or tested as a gateway.
